description: Guided traces for Week 4 including curriculum-calibrated Hard and Extra Rock levels; all snapshots are precomputed.

steps.explanation: Ready! Functions are defined first; their bodies run only when called.
Define greet; the body is saved but not run yet.
Call greet(). Jump to the function body.
Inside greet: print Hi. The function finishes and returns to the caller.
Ready! Functions are defined first; their bodies run only when called.
Define double(n). Nothing runs inside yet.
Call double(3) as the print argument.
Enter double with local parameter n = 3.
Return 3 * 2 = 6 to the print call.
The call has returned; print 6.
Ready! Functions are defined first; their bodies run only when called.
Define square(n).
Call square(4).
The local parameter n becomes 4.
Return n * n = 4 * 4 = 16.
Print 16 after the call returns.
Ready! Functions are defined first; their bodies run only when called.
Define add(a, b).
Call add(2, 5).
Assign parameters a = 2 and b = 5.
Return 2 + 5 = 7.
Print the returned value 7.

Define hello(). Its body is not executed because hello() is never called.
Print Done. The Hello line is skipped entirely.

Define square(n).
Prepare print(square(4) + 1): first call square(4).
Enter square with local n = 4.
Return 4 * 4 = 16.
Add 1 to the returned 16 and print 17.
Ready! Functions are defined first; their bodies run only when called.
Define subtract(a, b).
Call subtract(3, 10).
Set local a = 3, b = 10. Argument order matters.
Return 3 - 10 = -7.
Print -7.
Ready! Functions are defined first; their bodies run only when called.
Define greet(name).
Call greet('Mia') while calculating the right side of result = ...
Inside greet, the local parameter name is 'Mia'.
Print Hello Mia. This function has no return statement.
The function ends and implicitly returns None; assign result = None.
Print result. The second output line is None.

Define double(n).
Define triple_double(n).
Call triple_double(2).
Inside triple_double, local n = 2.
To calculate return double(n) * 3, call double(2).
Inside double, local n = 2.
Return 2 * 2 = 4 to triple_double.
Continue triple_double: 4 * 3 = 12. Return 12.
Print the returned 12.
Ready! Functions are defined first; their bodies run only when called.
Define check(n).
Call check(5).
Inside check, n = 5.
Check n > 0: 5 > 0 is True.
Return Yes immediately. The later return No is skipped.
Print Yes.
